passage: In the staff room of the coaching centre, Mohit stared at the same line of the attendance sheet for a full minute. Sudha had joined as a trainer that Monday. Six years ago, in college, he had borrowed her lab file and lost it, then let the department believe she had been careless. She lost marks; he stayed silent. It still replayed at night. At tea break he said, "Sudha, can we talk? I lost your file in second year and never told you. I'm sorry. I know it cost you marks." She was quiet, then said, "I wondered." Mohit did not ask her to say it was fine. "If it helps, I can write to the department and set the record straight." She said she would think about it. Walking to the bus stop, he noticed the replay had gone quieter.

qa.q: What had Mohit done to Sudha's lab file six years ago?
qa.a: He borrowed her lab file and lost it, then let the department believe she had been careless.

qa.q: Why could Mohit not look away from the attendance sheet, and what was he feeling?
qa.a: Guilt over the lost file: it still replayed in his head at night, and seeing Sudha brought it back.

qa.q: What made Mohit's apology a sound one?
qa.a: He named what he did and what it cost her, did not ask to be told it was fine, and offered a way to repair it.

qa.q: How might Sudha see the apology after six years?
qa.a: Her reply of "I wondered" suggests she may have suspected all along and now feels acknowledged, though she wants time to decide about the offer.

grounding: A mistake from years ago still replays; Mohit owns the harm, apologises specifically, offers amends and then feels the guilt ease.
